1. Purpose

The SoLID forward-angle muon detector of the DDVCS proposal (iron + scintillator; the DDVCS / J/ψ lite setup in solid_gemc, solid_gemc/geometry/muon_moved) has to tell μ− from π− at 2–11 GeV. This study asks how well iron + scintillator detectors do that, and what helps more: more iron, or finer sampling of the same iron.

Four geometries are simulated standalone with Geant4 (gemc), 104 μ− and 104 π− each (105 for muon_fa_hcal), p flat in 2–11 GeV, at normal incidence just in front of the iron (Section 2). muon_fa is read with 3 and with 4 layers (the same events), which makes five setups with 72–180 cm of iron. muon_hybrid and muon_fa 3 layers have the same 108 cm of iron, so that pair compares the readout alone: a 36-layer stack against thick scintillator planes.

A muon crosses every layer as a minimum-ionizing particle (MIP); a pion usually showers. Each setup's muon ID requires a MIP-like signal in every scintillator it reads on its own and, for a 36-layer stack, a MIP-like total energy in few towers. The figure of merit is the fraction of pions that pass at the same muon efficiency, 95% in every 2 GeV momentum bin; the passing pions are sorted by why they pass: punch-through, a muon from pion decay, or shower leakage (Section 4.1).

2. Detectors and simulation

The four geometries (Figure 1):

  • muon_fa: the muon detector of the SoLID DDVCS proposal, 36 cm iron blocks each followed by a 5 cm scintillator plane. The proposal has 3 layers (and GEMs); here the GEMs are removed and a 4th layer is added, so muon_fa is read with 3 and with 4 layers.
  • muon_hcal: a hadron calorimeter alone, after the STAR HCAL: 36 layers of 20 mm iron + 3 mm scintillator (72 cm iron), read as the energy summed over all layers in 10 × 10 cm towers.
  • muon_hybrid: muon_fa with its 2nd and 3rd layers replaced by the muon_hcal stack: iron block 1, scintillator 1, the stack, then a tail scintillator at the place of muon_fa scintillator 3. 108 cm of iron, the same as muon_fa 3 layers.
  • muon_fa_hcal: muon_fa layers 1–3 with the muon_hcal stack behind them, in place of muon_fa layer 4 (180 cm iron).

All detectors use the same simulation settings: no magnetic field, nothing upstream, physics list QGSP_BERT+STD+Optical with optical photons not recorded, and explicit random seeds per run. Edep is the true deposited energy from gemc: no light yield, Birks quenching or photostatistics. Momentum bins are 2 GeV wide; the gun stops at 11 GeV, so the last bin holds 10–11 GeV only.

muon_fa, 3 layers is not a separate geometry: it is scintillators 1–3 of the 4-layer runs with every scintillator-3 hit from a particle born in block 4 removed. Without that, block 4 sends particles from pion interactions back into scintillator 3 and makes the 3-layer reading look better than a detector that ends there (Section 5.6). A separate run of the 3-layer geometry agrees with the corrected reading.

π pass over 2–11 GeV with the cuts of a setup tuned so that 95% of muons pass in every 2 GeV p bin, 68% Clopper–Pearson interval; the efficiency reached over 2–11 GeV is next to it. Passing pions by Geant4 truth at the last read scintillator: P the pion itself crossed all the iron without a nuclear interaction (punch-through), M a muon from a pion decay got there, L neither (shower leakage). Floor: fraction of pions that cross all the iron without interacting. Last column: the simpler cuts of Figure 2b, where each cut variable alone keeps 98% of muons, so the muon efficiency of all cuts together differs by setup (Section 4.2).

  • Iron sets the limit. A pion that crosses all the iron without interacting is a MIP like a muon. That floor (Geant4 truth) falls about as exp(−LFe/18 cm): 1.6% at 72 cm, 0.2–0.3% at 108 cm, 0.06% at 144 cm, 0.003% at 180 cm. muon_hcal, with 72 cm, is dominated by it (158 of its 223 passing pions).
  • At equal iron (108 cm), muon_hybrid passes about half as many pions as muon_fa: 0.41% vs 0.88% (4.1σ); fewer at every muon efficiency from 90% to 97% and with either cut definition. The difference is shower leakage (11 vs 50 pions): the fine stack sees the shower that 5 cm scintillators behind 36 cm blocks miss. This holds for a beam hitting the stack centre at normal incidence; the muon_fa gun is a 10 cm disk.
  • More iron helps only where the readout can see the difference. A fourth muon_fa layer (144 cm) brings muon_fa to 0.23%. muon_fa_hcal (180 cm) removes nearly all punch-through (3 of 105) but passes 0.37%, more than the 4-layer muon_fa: 297 of its 368 passing pions interacted in the first 108 cm, and what reaches the stack leaves only a small signal there (6.3 MeV on average against 24.7 MeV for a muon), which a stack read as a sum over layers with upper cuts does not reject. For the same reason it keeps low-p muons that stop in the stack. Its pion pass falls with p (0.54% at 2–4 GeV, 0.19% at 10–11 GeV); above 4 GeV it is close to the 4-layer muon_fa (0.33% vs 0.28% ± 0.06%, Section 8).
  • Pion decay before the detector is not simulated, and in SoLID it is larger than every pass fraction here. A pion flies about 9.5 m from the target (z = −315 cm) to the muon iron (z = 620 cm). It decays on the way with probability L·mπ/(p·cτ) ≈ 0.17/p[GeV]: 8.5% at 2 GeV, 1.5% at 11 GeV, about 3% averaged over 2–11 GeV, against 0.2–2% pass fractions above. The decay muon is a real muon to any muon detector; it has to be rejected upstream (e.g. a kink or a momentum mismatch in the tracker, the EC), not by the iron.
  • Caveats. Normal incidence, the gun just in front of the iron (no upstream calorimeter), true deposited energy (no light yield or photostatistics), 104 pions per setup (±10–20% statistical on the pass fractions above, ±20–40% for the 4-layer muon_fa).

4. PID cut summary

4.1 What can still look like a muon

A muon at 2–11 GeV loses about 1.5 GeV in 108 cm of iron and leaves a MIP signal in every scintillator: about 10 MeV in 5 cm of plastic, about 0.7 MeV in a 3 mm stack layer. A pion that passes the muon ID is one of three kinds (Geant4 truth, at the last scintillator the setup reads):

  • P, punch-through: the pion crossed all the iron without a nuclear interaction. It is a MIP like a muon, so it passes at the muon rate; no cut on the signals removes it. Its fraction is the floor, counted from Geant4 truth for each setup (punch_lambda_v2.txt). All setups follow exp(−LFe/λFe − Lsc/λsc) with one iron length λFe ≈ 18.6 cm (simulated, 2–11 GeV; PDG gives 20.41 cm at 200 GeV/c) and a plastic term (λsc ≈ 50–100 cm, loosely constrained) for the scintillator Lsc the pion crosses before the last read one: 10.5 cm in 72 cm of muon_hcal against 5 cm in muon_fa. That accounts for part of the gap between muon_hcal's floor (1.60%) and muon_fa's at 72 cm (1.92%), about 6% of the 17% for λsc ≈ 90 cm; the rest is within statistics (about 1σ). A fit to the two stacks alone predicts the muon_fa floors 196, 26 and 3.5 (of 104) at 72, 108 and 144 cm against 192, 30 and 6 seen.
  • M, pion decay: a muon reached the last scintillator. Mostly the pion decayed before it interacted: the probability is λ·mπ/(p·cτ) ≈ 0.0033/p[GeV], 0.063% averaged over 2–11 GeV, and M is 0.059% for muon_fa_hcal and 0.05% for muon_fa 4 layers (at 95% muon efficiency); in the shallower setups (9–12 per 104 against ≈ 6) decays of pions from a shower add some. No calorimetric cut removes a muon.
  • L, shower leakage: the pion interacted, and its shower left a MIP-like signal in every readout layer. This is the part the readout design can reduce: more layers, finer segmentation, tracking.

4.2 The cuts of each setup

Every setup first requires a signal where a muon must leave one (a fixed threshold), then applies upper cuts that a MIP passes and a shower fails. The table gives the cut values of Figures 2b and 8b, where each cut variable alone keeps 98% of muons (Section 4.3).

Per layer or summed, for muon_fa? Cutting on the energy and hit count summed over the scintillators (2 cuts, with a hit still required in every scintillator) instead of per scintillator gives the same pion pass at equal muon efficiency: 3 layers 0.80% vs 0.88% at 95% and 1.13% vs 1.16% at 97%; 4 layers 0.21% vs 0.23% at 95% (pid_eq.C set 4, pid_eq_fasum.txt). Summed cuts only look better at 98% per cut variable because there are fewer of them: 97.6% of muons kept instead of 91%.

4.3 Two ways to set the cut values

Each cut variable alone keeps 98% of muons (Figures 2b, 8b). Each upper cut value is the 98th percentile of that one variable in the muon sample (all p), e.g. scintillator Edep < 27 MeV, ≤ 2 hits. A muon must pass every cut, so the overall muon efficiency is about 0.98n for n cuts (a little higher, since some muons fail several cuts together): muon_hcal 2 cuts → 98%, muon_hybrid 4 → 93%, muon_fa 3 layers 6 → 91%, 4 layers 8 → 88%, muon_fa_hcal 8 → 89%. A setup with more cuts then rejects more pions partly because it also loses more muons, so these numbers do not compare setups fairly.

Equal muon efficiency (Figures 2a, 2c, 8a, 8c, 16). To make the efficiency tunable, each hit or tower count is replaced by an energy with the same 1 MeV threshold (muon_fa: energy in hits beyond the two largest; stacks: energy in towers outside the best 2 × 2). Each cut value is the muon median vs p (a straight line through 1 GeV bins) plus an offset set separately in each 2 GeV p bin: in bin b all cuts of a setup use the same muon quantile qb, and each qb is tuned until the muon efficiency in that bin is 90, 93, 95 or 97%; the pion pass is compared there. The tracker gives p, so this is a cut a real detector can apply. Cut values come from the even-numbered muon events and qb is tuned on the odd ones, so the efficiency in every bin equals the target by construction; its statistical precision is about ±0.7% per bin for the 104-muon samples (±0.9% at 10–11 GeV) and ±0.2% for muon_fa_hcal. The muon_fa cuts reach 95.0–95.8% instead of 95.0%: the energy beyond the two largest hits is 0 for most muons, so that cut moves in steps. Pions never set a cut. A single bin's pion count also depends on how its cuts were tuned (the straight line through the muon medians uses all p): retuning on 4–11 GeV only (Section 8) moves single-bin counts by up to ±14 (muon_fa_hcal, 8–10 GeV: 72 instead of 58) while the 4–11 GeV totals change by at most 7 pions (muon_fa_hcal 254 vs 248), so read the totals, not single-bin differences, in Figures 2c, 8c and 16b. With one q for all p and the counts kept (q = 0.98), the same code reproduces Figures 2b and 8b exactly.

Why per p bin. With one q for all p, the efficiency at 95% over all p was 96–99% at 2–4 GeV and 92–93% at 10–11 GeV, because the muon signal tails widen with p. Per-bin cuts make it flat. The pion pass is unchanged for muon_fa, muon_hcal and muon_hybrid (88 vs 89, 23 vs 23, 223 vs 223, 41 vs 41 pions at 95%) and lower for muon_fa_hcal, 0.37% instead of 0.42%: its pion pass falls steeply with p, so moving muon efficiency from low p to high p removes more pions than it admits (pid_eq.C set 8, pid_eq_perbin.txt).

Pion pass over 2–11 GeV at each muon efficiency, the same in every 2 GeV p bin (Figure 2a; muon_fa 4 layers: Figure 8a). 68% intervals in pid_eq_L123.txt and pid_eq_fa4.txt. The P column matches εμ × the truth number of pions that cross all the iron in every setup, as it should for pions that are MIPs. The 97% column sits at the edge of the muon samples: for the 104-muon setups it is set by the tail of about 550 test muons in the 10–11 GeV bin (above 4 GeV only, the 4-layer muon_fa cannot reach 97% in every bin at all).

At 108 cm muon_hybrid passes about half as many pions as muon_fa 3 layers at 95%, fewer from 90% to 97%, and with either cut definition (95%: 41 vs 88, 4.1σ; integer-count cuts with one q for all p, 95%: 40 vs 89; 97%: 48 vs 101). The difference is shower leakage (11 vs 50). Part of the rest is the floor, 20 vs 30 pions reaching the last scintillator without interacting (1.4σ apart, so not established). muon_hybrid is flat from 90% to 97% because 30 of its 41 passing pions are punch-through or decays, which no cut removes. The stack runs used a pencil beam on a tower centre and muon_fa a 10 cm disk, so this is for central impact. At 72 cm there is no clean muon_fa sample to compare with muon_hcal: its scintillator 1+2 reading has 72 cm of unread iron behind it (Section 5.6).

4.5 What each cut does, and what did not help

  • Removing one cut at a time (equal-efficiency cuts, 95% per bin): the hit-count and outside-the-2×2 cuts do the work. Without the muon_hybrid stack's outside-2×2 cut 23 more pions pass; without the front, Etot or tail energy cut only 1–3 more pass, but each of those costs 1.1–1.6 points of muon efficiency. In muon_fa (3 layers) each MIP Edep cut lets back 5–13 pions and costs 0.6–0.9 points. Dropping those cuts and retuning is not done yet.
  • muon_fa cuts on the sums over scintillators instead of per scintillator: the same pion pass at equal muon efficiency within statistics (Section 4.2).
  • Shifting each cut value with the muon median vs p alone (one quantile q for all p) changes nothing: the median moves by only 0.04 MeV per GeV in a muon_fa scintillator, and it does not flatten the muon efficiency vs p, because the muon tails, not the median, widen with p. A separate quantile per 2 GeV bin does (Section 4.3).
  • Energies instead of counts, with the same 1 MeV thresholds, are not better than the counts in general (counts: one q for all p): at 95% 88 vs 89 pions for muon_fa 3 layers, 41 vs 40 for muon_hybrid, but 223 vs 215 for muon_hcal; worse at 97% for muon_fa (116 vs 101) and muon_fa_hcal (668 vs 441 of 105), and at 90% for muon_hcal (205 vs 182, since the outside-2×2 cut allows four towers where the count allowed two); better at 95% for muon_fa_hcal (368 vs 400). Their gain is that the efficiency can be set exactly. An idealized version on truth deposits with no threshold passed far fewer pions (on the separate 3-layer muon_fa runs, 0.56% instead of 0.75% at 93%; scint 1+2 0.99% instead of 2.6%), a hint that the readout threshold matters; that is a hardware question and not pursued. It was found after trying three muon_fa variable sets on the same pions, so it is only a hint.
next
  • A lower cut on the summed stack energy (a muon that crosses all 36 layers leaves about 25 MeV) against the pions that pass muon_fa_hcal with a small stack signal (Section 8); it would also remove muons that stop in the stack.
  • Drop the cuts that cost muons and reject almost nothing (muon_hybrid front, Etot and tail energy) and retune.
  • muon_fa: straight-track alignment across the layers and timing, against the remaining shower leakage.
  • Target-pointing angles instead of normal incidence; EC FA upstream, since in SoLID most pions shower there first; pion decay in flight upstream of the detector (not simulated: the gun sits just in front of the iron).
  • GEM hit multiplicity (on hold).

5. muon_fa: 4 layers, 144 cm Fe

5.1 How deep each particle gets

Every muon reaches all four scintillators. Pions leave a hit in scintillator 1 in 82–99% of events, in scintillator 2 (behind 72 cm Fe) in 23–61%, in scintillator 3 (108 cm) in 5–21%, and in scintillator 4 (144 cm) in 1–4%. All rise with p as the shower gets more energetic.

5.5 Using fewer layers

Figure 8 shows the same events read on fewer scintillators: (b) with the same per-layer cut values, (a) and (c) at equal muon efficiency.

At 95% muon efficiency in each p bin: 3.35% (1+2), 1.48% (2+3), 0.69% (1+2+3) and 0.23% (1–4). Each layer matters. With scintillators 1+2 the pass fraction (2.7%) is dominated by its 1.92% floor. At 95% muon efficiency, dropping scintillator 1 but keeping all 108 cm of iron raises the pass fraction 2.1×, from 0.69% to 1.48% (both readings have block 4 behind them), at the same floor: scintillator 1 sees the showers that start in the first iron block. Without it, probably, a pion that interacts there and sends one MIP-like hadron through scintillators 2 and 3 passes (not checked with truth). The fourth layer takes muon_fa 3 layers (no splash-back) from 0.88% to 0.23% at 95% muon efficiency; with each cut variable alone at 98% of muons, from 0.62% at 91% to 0.18% at 88% muon efficiency (the table's 1+2+3 column, 0.41%, is the raw reading with block 4 behind it). The 1+2, 2+3 and 1+2+3 readings have unread iron behind them, which rejects some punch-through pions (Section 5.6), so they are better than detectors that end there.

Cut values are integers for the hit count. They are the 98% quantile of the muon sample, so a small change in the muon sample can flip one, e.g. ≤ 3 instead of ≤ 2 hits in scintillator 2. On these runs, the cut values taken from the muons of the separate 3-layer runs (that flip, and Edep cuts 0.6–1 MeV higher) give 3.30% for scintillators 1+2 instead of 2.70%. Compare configurations at equal muon efficiency or with the same cut values; Figures 8a, 8c and Section 4 do that.

5.6 Iron behind the last read scintillator

Pions that cross the iron without interacting (P) should pass the muon cuts at the muon rate. They do when nothing follows the last read scintillator, and they do not when more iron follows it (cuts with integer counts and one q for all p, at 95% muon efficiency, 96% for scintillators 1+2 where an integer step overshoots; so the counts differ by a few from Section 4.4, which uses energies):

ReadingBehind the last read scintillatorP passingexpected εμ × P
muon_fa scint 1+2blocks 3 and 4 (72 cm)117184
muon_fa scint 1–3, 4-layer runsblock 4 (36 cm)2028.5
muon_fa scint 1–3, 4-layer runs, scintillator-3 hits born behind it removedblock 4, its splash-back removed2828.6
muon_fa scint 2+3, 4-layer runsblock 4 (36 cm)1428.5
muon_fa scint 1–3, separate 3-layer runsnothing2727.5
muon_fa scint 1–4nothing65.7
muon_hybrid tailnothing1719.0
muon_hcal last layernothing156152.0

So reading a subset of the 4-layer muon_fa describes a detector with unread iron behind it, not one that ends there. The mechanism is splash-back: the pion's interaction in the next block sends particles back into the last scintillator, which then fails the hit-count cut (removing that cut for scintillator 3 lets 7 of these back in). Truth check (splash_check.C, splash_check.txt): for the 24 punch-through pions that interact in block 4, scintillator 3 gets on average 34 MeV from tracks other than the pion, 47% of it from tracks moving backward, and 67% of these events have more than two hits there; for the 6 that cross block 4 it is 1.5 MeV and none; on the 3-layer runs 1 of 29. Within one sample the effect is clear: on the 4-layer runs, the punch-through pions whose primary also crosses the next block all pass (6 of 6 at scintillator 3, 30 of 30 at scintillator 2), and those that interact in it pass far less often (14 of 24 and 87 of 162). Decay muons (M) are also fewer than on the 3-layer runs (9 vs 16, 1.4σ, not significant); shower leakage (L) is the same (43 vs 41).

Closure test (pid_eq.C set 6, pid_eq_backcut.txt): on the 4-layer runs, drop every scintillator-3 hit whose track, mother or any recorded earlier ancestor was born behind scintillator 3 (vertex z > 757.5 cm, its back face; block 4 starts at 758 cm). This removes 19.5% of the pion Edep in scintillator 3 and 0.4% of the muon Edep. Scintillators 1–3 of the 4-layer runs then reproduce the 3-layer runs at 95% muon efficiency: 0.89% vs 0.84% (integer counts) and 0.88% vs 0.93% (energies, per p bin); with integer counts P 28 vs 27, M 10 vs 16, L 51 vs 41, and 22 of the 24 pions that interact in block 4 now pass (14 before). The same cut on the 3-layer runs changes nothing. So, within statistics, splash-back from block 4 explains the difference; M (10 vs 16) and L (51 vs 41) differ by about 1σ each, in opposite directions. This corrected reading is the muon_fa 3 layers of Figure 2 and Sections 2–4. Following only the hit's own track and its mother recovers most of it.

5.7 What still passes

6 of the 104 pions (0.06%) cross all 144 cm of Fe without an inelastic interaction (Geant4 truth, punch_lambda_v2.txt); behind 108 cm it is 30 (0.30%). They are minimum-ionizing like muons, so about 88% of the 6, roughly 5, are expected to pass cut D, which passes 18. By Geant4 truth, at 95% muon efficiency in each p bin 23 pions pass: 6 punch-through, 5 with a muon reaching scintillator 4, and 12 shower leakage (pid_eq_fa4.txt). Straight-track alignment across the layers, or timing, would target the leakage part.

6.3 What limits it

160 of the 104 pions (1.60%) cross all 72 cm of Fe without interacting (Geant4 truth), an effective length of 17.4 cm for the iron and the 10.5 cm of plastic together (Section 4.1). Such a pion is a MIP in every layer and no cut on Etot or tower count can remove it; with 98% of them expected to pass, they make about 157 of the 234 passing pions, two thirds. The remaining ≈ 77 interact and still look muon-like, or bring a muon to the last layer. At 95% muon efficiency in each p bin with the equal-efficiency cuts, 223 pass: 158 punch-through, 9 with a muon and 56 shower leakage (Section 4.4). Only more iron lowers the floor.

Each part alone is weak: the front scintillator passes 37% and the stack 26%, because many pions shower in the front 36 cm of iron and leave little in the stack. They work only together with the tail requirement. Each bin holds about 2200 pions, so the per-bin "all" values rest on 5–11 events.

7.3 What passes, and more variables

20 of the 104 pions (0.20%) reach the tail without interacting. To see whether muon_hybrid's extra information helps, hybrid_pid2.C adds, with cut values per 2 GeV bin from one half of the muon sample: the hit count in the front and tail scintillators (2 cm clustering), the distance between the front and tail hit positions (each smeared by the assumed 2 cm resolution), the stack energy outside the 3 × 3 towers the front hit points to, and a lower Etot cut. The selection was set on the earlier 30-layer muon_hybrid runs and then applied once to these runs.

muon_hybrid, 36-layer stack (these runs)0.40%0.38%0.20%

The gain is about 2 pions, not significant. These are hybrid_pid2.C's own cuts (values per 2 GeV bin, its own muon split), so its numbers differ by a few from Section 4.4 (41 pions, 18 / 12 / 11, at 95%). Of the 38 pions that pass it with the added variables at 92.7% muon efficiency, 19 are punch-through primaries, 11 have a muon in the tail and only 8 are shower leakage, so no further cut on these variables has much left to remove. With exact (unsmeared) positions the front–tail match is tighter and gives 0.33%, so a tracking resolution well below 2 cm would help a little. Numbers in hybrid_pid2_L36.txt.

8. muon_fa_hcal: muon_fa layers 1–3 + the muon_hcal stack (180 cm Fe)

muon_fa iron blocks and scintillators 1–3 exactly as in the 4-layer muon_fa, then, where block 4 was (z = 758 cm), the 36-layer muon_hcal stack (1 × 1 m, 72 cm Fe) centred on the beam (x = 180 cm). 105 μ− and 105 π−, same gun as muon_fa. The stack is read like muon_hcal, only as energy summed over its 36 layers in 10 × 10 cm towers (study rule). The cuts are those of muon_fa on scintillators 1–3 plus the stack's Etot and tower count, with some energy required in the stack.

At 95% muon efficiency in each p binIronπ passingpunch-through Ppion decay Mleakage L
muon_fa_hcal180 cm0.37% (368 / 105)0.003%0.059%0.306%
muon_fa, 4 layers144 cm0.23% (23 / 104)0.06%0.05%0.12%
muon_hybrid108 cm0.41%0.18%0.12%0.11%
muon_fa, 3 layers108 cm0.88%0.28%0.10%0.50%

At 95% muon efficiency in each p bin muon_fa_hcal passes 0.37%, more than the 4-layer muon_fa (0.23%) and less than muon_hybrid (0.41%). At 90% it is close to the 4-layer muon_fa (0.20% vs 0.18%); towards 97% it rises fast (0.67%; integer-count cuts do better there, 0.44%, Section 4.5). The extra iron removes the punch-through (3 of 105); 306 of the 368 passing pions are shower leakage. Tuning the cuts per p bin instead of once for all p lowered its pion pass from 0.42% to 0.37% (Section 4.3).

What these pions are (Geant4 truth, a diagnostic only, not a cut; pid_eq_fahcal.txt). 297 of the 306 interacted in the first 108 cm of iron; only 9 had the primary still at scintillator 3. The particle with the largest signal in scintillator 3 is a proton (95), an electron (79), a π− (36), a neutron (31) or a muon (30). Whatever reaches the stack leaves little there: mean Etot 6.3 MeV against 24.7 MeV for a passing muon, and only 15 of the 306 deposit anything (> 0.2 MeV) beyond stack layer 32, against 96% of the muons. A stack read only as a sum over layers cannot see that depth, and its cuts are upper cuts, so a signal smaller than a muon's passes. For the same reason the muons that stop in the stack (below about 2.4–2.5 GeV/c, muon_eloss.C) still pass, so 95% of muons can be kept at 2–4 GeV as at 10–11 GeV; the pion pass falls with p, from 0.54% at 2–4 GeV to 0.19% at 10–11 GeV.

Above 4 GeV (pid_eq.C set 7, pid_eq_p4.txt; every setup's cuts tuned to 95% in each p bin of 4–11 GeV): muon_fa_hcal 0.33%, muon_fa 4 layers 0.28%, muon_hybrid 0.45%, muon_fa 3 layers 1.02%, muon_hcal 2.16%. muon_fa_hcal and the 4-layer muon_fa are equal there within the 4-layer's ±0.06%.

Counts are the 105-event muon_fa_hcal sample against 104 for the others, so the 4-layer muon_fa numbers have about ±20–40% statistical errors. Like muon_hcal, the stack runs hit the stack centre; a beam near a tower edge is not tested.

10. Methodology

Simulation

Each run is bin/solid-gemc-run run study/muon_study/<gcard> study/muon_study, with this folder as gemc's run folder. The muon_fa geometry is a renamed copy of muon_moved with a 4th iron block and scintillator added by hand; muon_hcal and muon_hybrid are generated by muon_hcal.pl and muon_hybrid.pl. Each scintillator is a flux detector: muon_fa ids 6101000–6104000, muon_hcal ids 7000001–7000036, muon_hybrid front 7100000, stack 7100001–7100036 and tail 7100037. All have 0 overlaps.

Analysis

mu_pi_compare.C (muon_fa, 6th argument = number of layers, 4 here) works per event:

  • Edep per layer is the sum of totEdep over all tracks.
  • A layer is hit at Edep > 5 MeV. For hit counting, track deposits within 2 cm in x–y (avg_x, avg_y) are merged, and a cluster above 1 MeV is one hit. The two thresholds come from a threshold scan: a high layer threshold removes faint shower debris, a low cluster threshold keeps the small extra hits that mark a shower (mu_pi_thrscan.txt, result.md).

hcal_mu_pi.C (muon_hcal, 4th argument 36) puts each deposit in a 10×10 cm tower by its track's average position, summed over all 36 layers; the 11 × 11 grid is shifted by half a tower so the pencil beam hits a tower center. A tower above 1 MeV counts. Etot is the sum of all towers.

hybrid_mu_pi.C (muon_hybrid, 4th argument 36) reads the front and tail scintillators with a 5 MeV hit threshold, and sums the 36-layer stack into the same 11 × 11 towers.

All three bin in the generated momentum and set cut values at the 98% quantile of the muon sample. Outputs: fa4_mu_pi_1e4.*, hcal36_mu_pi_1e4.* and hybrid36_mu_pi_1e4.*, plus the *_final.root files that compare3.C plots. punch_lambda.C (output punch_lambda_v2.txt) counts the floor from Geant4 truth: a pion event whose primary (track id 1) reaches a scintillator had no inelastic interaction.

pid_eq.C rebuilds the same variables for all configs from out.root and compares them at equal muon efficiency (Section 4.3): set 0 makes Figures 2a and 2c (and the muon_fa 3-layer and muon_fa_hcal inputs of Figure 2b), set 1 Figures 8a and 8c, set 2 the 3-layer vs 4-layer muon_fa check (pid_eq_fa3check.txt), set 4 muon_fa per-layer vs summed cuts (pid_eq_fasum.txt), set 6 the vertex-z closure test of Section 5.6 (pid_eq_backcut.txt), set 3 Figure 16 (muon_fa_hcal, with the truth diagnostic of its passing pions), set 7 all setups at p ≥ 4 GeV (pid_eq_p4.txt), set 8 per-bin vs one-q-for-all-p cuts at 95% (pid_eq_perbin.txt). muon_fa_hcal geometry: muon_fa3__geometry_Original.txt (the 4-layer muon_fa without block 4) and muon_fa_hcal.pl (the stack, ids 7200001–7200036, 0 overlaps). The pion truth class comes from the flux hits in the last read scintillator: track id 1 with |pid| = 211 (P), else any |pid| = 13 (M), else L. No muon ID cut uses Geant4 truth. The cut variables come only from the detector id, the deposited energy (totEdep) and the hit position (avg_x, avg_y) of the flux hits, and the momentum bins and p-dependent cut values from the generated p (a stand-in for the tracker momentum); this holds for pid_eq.C, mu_pi_compare.C, hcal_mu_pi.C, hybrid_mu_pi.C and hybrid_pid2.C. Truth (track id, particle type, vertices) is used only to label passing pions P/M/L, to count the floor, and to remove the splash-back for muon_fa 3 layers, which stands in for a detector that ends after scintillator 3. Two readout idealizations remain: hits are the energy-weighted positions of individual tracks, merged within 2 cm, which assumes a position-sensitive readout; and Edep has no light yield or photostatistics. In the text files the cut sets are named OLD (integer counts, one cut value for all p, as Figure 2b), OLDs (OLD with cut values shifted with the muon median vs p), NEW (OLDs with counts replaced by energies, one q for all p) and NEWb (NEW with a separate q per 2 GeV p bin, its target the efficiency in every bin; Figures 2a, 2c, 8a, 8c, 16 and all equal-efficiency numbers). muon_fa 3 layers (pid_eq.C kind 5): scintillators 1–3 of the 4-layer runs, dropping scintillator-3 hits whose track, mother or a recorded ancestor (mtid chain) has a vertex z > 757.5 cm.
